note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 description of Eutermes Ilinquipatensis (in German, the genus spelled thus in the original); the species was named by Holmgren in 1906 and is redescribed in that work, including the alate, soldier and worker. Type locality Llinquipata, Puno, Peru. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A small species: soldier head length only 1.33 mm, head width 0.74 mm, body length about 4 mm; nasus very thick and relatively very long, the frontal outline perfectly straight; alate head nearly circular, compound eyes medium-sized and displaced somewhat dorsally, ocelli strongly prominent.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Colour and bristles as in E. chaquimayensis. Head nearly circular; compound eyes medium-sized, displaced somewhat dorsally; ocelli perfectly circular and strongly prominent, rather close to the compound eyes; head capsule sutures faintly visible; frontal marks very small; the muscle scars at the transverse band forming a flat arc in front of the frontal marks; mandibular bare process large. Base of the postclypeus short. Antennae (15) segments: segment 3 either only very slightly longer than segment 2 (which equals segment 4), or far longer than segment 2 and divided into a shorter basal and a longer terminal part. Anterior margin of the pronotum straight with a weak median notch, the length half its width; posterior margin distinctly concave in the middle. Posterior margin of the mesonotum more deeply concave than that of the metanotum. Measurements: head length 1.64 mm; from the anterior margin of the transverse band to the occiput 0.96 mm (the body length and head width figures are blurred in the OCR and are not cited).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish brown, anterior margin of the pronotum brownish; body weakly yellowish brown, antennae yellowish, legs white to straw-yellow. Head densely covered with very fine hairs and with longer bristles at the base of the nasus and on the vertex; abdominal tergites with fine hairs and longer bristles at the posterior margin, the sternites additionally long-haired. Nasus very thick and relatively very long; frontal outline perfectly straight. Antennae 12 or 13-segmented. Pronotum not strongly saddle-shaped, anterior margin not concave. Measurements: body length about 4 mm; head length 1.33 mm; head width 0.74 mm.
